note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 5510 / 出力 1947 トークン

data.question: Should hold_limit be raised from 50s back to 60s, a partial revert of D4, as the mitigation for company C promised in D1 and D4, even though the measurement shows it is slightly worse for customers in this period?
data.background: The purpose of this change is fairness to company C, which the operator committed to in D1 and D4 but which the KPI does not name. Measured on the same seeds, it does not improve the main goal (-0.2, 0/5 seeds) and it worsens customers' tail waits. Trading customer outcomes for company fairness, and deciding whether hold_limit should differ by season or demand level, is a value judgment for the operator, not something I should settle by applying the KPI alone.

options.summary: Raise hold_limit from 50s to 60s. Measured result: on-time 81.0 -> 80.8 (-0.2, 0/5 seeds improved), late 1.6 -> 1.8, p95_wait_s 94.6 -> 116, max_wait_s 270 -> 321, unfinished stays 0.0, blocked s 888 -> 1046, road violations 27.2 -> 26.0, lowest on-time rate stays 0.96. Utility A / B / C 25.4 / 25.7 / 8.9 -> 25.2 / 25.4 / 10.2. It passes check, the constitution and the KPI conditions, and A, B and C all vote yes. It would not clear the +1.0 objective gate.
options.stakeholders: C gains (+1.3 utility, about 15% of its current level), which partly honours the D1/D4 commitment. A (-0.2) and B (-0.3) lose a little but agree. Customers lose: the slowest waits get longer (p95 +21s, max +51s) and late deliveries rise slightly, with no gain in on-time deliveries. Road violations fall slightly, which benefits other road users.

options.summary: Stay at v3 (hold_limit 50s). On-time 81.0, late 1.6, p95_wait_s 94.6, max_wait_s 270, unfinished 0.0, blocked s 888, road violations 27.2. Utility A / B / C stays 25.4 / 25.7 / 8.9.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current, better tail waits. A and B keep their current utility. C stays far behind (8.9 compared with about 25 for A and B), and the mitigation promised in D1 and D4 is delayed again, which costs C's trust and the operator's credibility.

recommendation.reason: The KPI is about customers, and option 1 is measured as worse for them: p95_wait_s rises from 94.6 to 116, max_wait_s from 270 to 321, late from 1.6 to 1.8, and no seed improves on-time deliveries. This is the same customer-for-fairness trade that D4 rejected. Even with a unanimous vote, customers do not vote, and the KPI asks that changes worse for them be justified. A fairness gain of +1.3 for C does not supply that justification. The D1/D4 commitment to C is real. It should be met through a mitigation that does not cost customers, such as negotiated compensation or a rule aimed at C's bottleneck, or through an intermediate value such as 55s measured per seed. Option 1 can also be revisited in a high-demand period, where the trade-off may differ.
assumptions: The 5-seed measurement represents the current quiet-period demand.
The rise in p95_wait_s and max_wait_s is mainly caused by the longer hold_limit and is not seed noise.
The operator still does not count company fairness as a KPI goal (K1).

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: No rule change; expected to stay around 81.0 under the same demand.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: Stays around 94.6 instead of rising to 116.

predictions.subject: metric:max_wait_s
predictions.note: Stays around 270 instead of rising to 321.

predictions.subject: metric:utility@C
predictions.note: C stays around 8.9; the mitigation remains outstanding.

unknowns: Per-seed spread of p95_wait_s and max_wait_s, and whether the increase holds on every seed or is driven by a few outliers.
How an intermediate hold_limit (e.g. 55s) performs for customers and for C.
Why C's utility is so low (8.9): the cause of its bottleneck and whether a rule can target it directly.
Each company's future behaviour policy, and how C will react to a further delay of the promised mitigation.
Next period's demand level, and whether a longer hold_limit helps or hurts in busy periods (the basis for any seasonal setting).
How customers perceive longer worst-case waits when deliveries still arrive within the promised time.
Whether the small drop in road violations (27.2 -> 26.0) matters for safety; the cause of the violation level has been unexamined since D1.
